title: Beyond Real or Fake: A Dual-Channel Authenticity and Reasoning Protocol for Photographic Assessment
claim: Authenticity cues split into two channels whose corruption pattern identifies the manipulation type, and a dual-channel pipeline exploits this to classify and explain.
layout: 3 panels: taxonomy pipes on top, classifier and evidence loop below, left-to-right
description: The top panel (a) shows two horizontal pipes, a blue camera channel and an orange semantic channel. Their outputs feed four dashed boxes: footprint-preserved transformations, GenAI retouching, GenAI tampering and fully synthetic. Each box shows small pipe icons marked preserved (green check), corrupted or locally corrupted (red X or warning), so each manipulation has its own signature. A dash-dot line separates this from the bottom half. Bottom-left panel (b) is the classifier. A reference photo goes to a semantic encoder (frozen) and a camera encoder, both into a green Fusion block, then an Authenticity? diamond. Bottom-right panel (c) takes a verified reference and a query photo through encoders, giving S_sem and S_cam gauges and saliency heatmaps. These form a privileged two-channel context for a frozen VLM. A Consistent? diamond loops back through Rethink & Revise, then outputs an explanation and a localized red box. Peach and green backgrounds separate (b) and (c).
caption: \textbf{\method{} overview.} (a) Two-channel taxonomy. Authenticity cues are decoupled into a camera channel $C_{\mathrm{cam}}$ (sensor traces) and a semantic channel $C_{\mathrm{sem}}$ (scene coherence); each manipulation type leaves a distinct signature: footprint-preserved transformations preserve both channels, GenAI retouching corrupts only $C_{\mathrm{cam}}$, GenAI tampering corrupts $C_{\mathrm{cam}}$ globally and $C_{\mathrm{sem}}$ locally, and fully synthetic images corrupt both. (b) Authenticity classification (Q1). A camera encoder (Sec. [ref]) and a frozen semantic encoder feed a cross-attention fusion module with learnable reliability weights (Sec. [ref]) that produces a four-class verdict (Sec. [ref]). (c) Reference-based evidence generation (Q2). Given a query $\xq$ and a camera-verified reference $\xref$, the two encoders yield channel alignment scores $\scam, \ssem$ (Eq. [ref]) and a patch-level saliency map (Eq. [ref]); these serve as privileged two-channel context to a frozen VLM in an Observe-Generate-Refine loop (Sec. [ref]) that returns an explanation and localization, revising whenever the VLM's initial assessment is inconsistent with the channel evidence (Sec. [ref]).
abstract: Forensic verification has converged on a binary "real vs. fake" label that confates fully synthetic, tampered, and AI-retouched images despite their very different consequences. We argue that GenAI manipulations decompose along two complementary channels: a camera channel of sensor fingerprints (destroyed by neural processing), and a semantic channel of scene-level coherence (disrupted by content edits). Each manipulation type leaves a distinctive two-channel signature. We instantiate this taxonomy in 2CAP (2-Channel Authenticity Protocol), pairing a contrastively-trained camera encoder with a frozen semantic encoder to serve two applications on a shared backbone: (i) four-class authenticity classification via cross-attention fusion with learnable reliability weights; and (ii) evidence generation, where an authentic image serves as a reference for a query and the two encoders produce per-channel alignment scores together with a patch-level saliency map. These signals are supplied as privileged context to a frozen Vision-Language Model (VLM) through an Observe-Generate-Refine loop, yielding explanations with localization without forensic fine-tuning. On a multi-source benchmark, 2CAP attains the best classification performance, including strong retouching detection where existing methods fail, and improves explanation quality.
